OBITUARY REFERENCE
MR. CHAIRMAN : Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing
away of Shri Vishwanath Pratap Singh, former Prime Minister of India.
Shri Vishwanath Pratap Singh, who was ailing for quite some time passed away on
27th November, 2008 at the age of 77 years. Born in Allahabad in June 1931, Shri
Singh had his education at the Allahabad University and the Pune University.
From his student days, Shri Singh was active in politics and served as the President
of the Student’s Union of his college in Varanasi and was the Vice-President of the
Allahabad University Students’ Union. He took part in the Bhoodan Movement in
1957 and donated a well-established farm in village Pasna, District Allahabad, owned
by him. Shri Singh was also the founder of the Gopal Vidyalaya and an Intermediate
College at Karaon in Allahabad.
Shri Singh had a long and illustrious political career that started with the
membership of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly, where he served twice from
1969 to 1971 and then from 1981 to 1983. He was also Member of the Legislative
Council of Uttar Pradesh from 1980 to 1981. Shri Singh served as the Chief Minister
of Uttar Pradesh from 1980 to 1982. As Chief Minister, he took several steps for the
welfare of the people of Uttar Pradesh and also dealt with the menace of dacoits in
that State.

[RAJYA SABHA]2
Shri Singh represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in Rajya Sabha from July 1983
to April, 1988 and was the Leader of the House from December 1984 to April 1987. He
was also elected to the Fifth, Seventh, Ninth and Tenth Lok Sabha. He served as the
Union Deputy Minister of Commerce from 1974 to 1976, Minister of State for Commerce
from 1976 to 1977, Minister of Commerce with additional charge of the Department of
Supply and Industry from 1983 to 1984, Minister of Finance from 1984 to 1987 with
additional charge of Commerce and Supply from January 1985 to March 1985; and
Minister of Defence from January 1987 to April 1987.
Shri Singh occupied the Office of the Prime Minister of India from December 1989
to November 1990 and would always be remembered for his commitment to the
realisation of social justice.
Shri Singh was a poet at heart and his first anthology of poems was published
under the title ‘Ek Tukra Dharti, Ek Tukra Aasman’ . He was fond of painting and
photography and had also held exhibitions of his artwork.
In the passing away Shri Vishwanath Pratap Singh, the country has lost a patriot,
a great statesman, a veteran Parliamentarian and an able administrator.
I request hon. Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of
respect to the memory of the departed.
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
MR CHAIRMAN : Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved
family our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.
REFERENCE BY THE CHAIR
The Victims of Terrorist Attacks in Mumbai and Bomb Blasts in Assam
MR. CHAIRMAN : The city of Mumbai has faced unprecedented and heinous
terrorist attacks that have led to the killing of 164 people, including 26 foreign nationals
and 18 security personnel, and have injured 308 people.
Hon. Members are also aware of the serial blasts that occured in various districts
of Assam on 30th October that have killed 89 innocent people and injured 447 others.
These dastardly attacks have deeply shocked the nation and are aimed at
destablizing the country. Such incidents unite all citizens and strengthen our resolve
to continue on our path of national development. The scourge of terrorism must be
countered at all levels by the people and the Government.
This House salutes the bravery and dedication of security officials and others who
laid down their lives in the line of duty and expresses deepest condolences of the
families of those killed and injured in the attacks.
I request hon. Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these terrorist attacks.
